result.what_interviewer_wanted: Explain why a mutable default argument is dangerous, including that defaults are evaluated once at definition time and shared across calls, and how to avoid it.
result.improved_answer: A mutable default argument is dangerous because the default value is evaluated only once when the function is defined, so the same list instance is reused on every call. This means that if the function mutates the list, those changes persist across subsequent calls, leading to unexpected behavior. The usual fix is to use `None` as the default and create a new list inside the function body.
